title: The red crayon
text: You and Meera both want the red crayon. You get it first. Meera looks sad. She wanted to colour a red apple. What do you do?

options.text: Use it quickly, then give it to Meera
options.consequence: Meera waits. Soon her apple is red too.

options.text: Keep it. I got it first
options.consequence: You colour happily. Meera sits quietly with no red.
options.why: Meera felt left out and could not finish her apple. Maybe you two can both use the crayon?

options.text: Hide the crayon in my bag
options.consequence: Meera looks everywhere. Now nobody is colouring.
options.why: Hiding it made Meera feel upset, and drawing stopped. Maybe there is a way you both can colour?

hint.text: What did Meera want to colour?

title: The wet drawing
text: Kabir walks past your desk. Your water bottle falls and wets your drawing. Kabir stops and looks at the puddle. Did he mean it? What do you do?

options.consequence: "Sorry! My bag hit it," Kabir says. He helps you wipe it.

options.text: Shout at Kabir and push him
options.consequence: Kabir looks shocked. The teacher comes, and you both feel bad.

options.text: Wipe it and stay quiet all day
options.consequence: The drawing dries a little, but you feel upset all day.

hint.text: Do you know yet if Kabir did it on purpose?

title: Hot face at the swings
text: You were waiting for the swing. Riya runs and takes it first. Your face feels hot. Your hands make fists. What do you do?

options.consequence: Your hands relax. Now you can think about what to say.
Riya slips onto the sand and starts to cry.
The angry feeling stays, and you miss your turn.

hint.text: What is your body telling you?

title: Ice cream after dinner
text: Papa bought ice cream. He says, "We will eat it after dinner." The freezer is right there. Papa is busy on the phone. What do you do?

options.consequence: Dinner comes fast. Then everyone has ice cream together.

options.text: Eat a big spoon now, quietly
options.consequence: It is yummy, but Papa finds the open box later.
options.why: Taking a spoon meant Papa found the open box later. How might Papa feel now?

options.text: Ask Papa, "Can I have some now?"
options.consequence: Papa says, "After dinner," and you wait a long time.

hint.text: What could you do so you don't think about it?

title: The broken cup
text: You are playing ball inside. The ball hits Mummy's cup and it breaks. Nobody saw. Mummy calls, "What was that noise?" What do you do?

options.consequence: Mummy looks sad about her cup, but thanks you for telling her.
Mummy looks at the sleepy cat. Your tummy feels heavy.
options.why: Blaming the cat leaves you feeling worried inside. Maybe sharing what really happened would help you feel lighter?

options.text: Hide the pieces under the sofa
options.consequence: Later Mummy finds them and is upset nobody told her.
options.why: Hiding the cup made Mummy sad later. Maybe telling her what happened could help fix things together?

hint.text: How would you want someone to tell you?

title: Alone at lunch
text: Tenzin is new. He speaks only a little Hindi. He sits alone at lunch. Your friends say, "Don't sit with him." What do you do?

options.text: Tell my friends, "Tenzin can sit with us!"
options.consequence: One friend frowns, but Tenzin smiles and sits with you.
Tenzin eats alone again. He looks at the floor.
options.why: Tenzin still has nobody to sit with at lunch. How might Tenzin feel right now?

options.text: Tell the teacher Tenzin is alone
options.consequence: The teacher helps Tenzin find a place to sit.

hint.text: How might Tenzin feel, sitting alone?

title: Lost at the market
text: You are at the market with Papa. You stop to look at balloons. Now you cannot see Papa! What do you do?

options.text: Stay here and ask the shopkeeper
options.consequence: The shopkeeper calls out loudly. Papa hurries back and holds your hand.
Everything looks different, and it is harder to find Papa.
options.why: Running moves you farther away from where Papa last saw you. Maybe staying in one spot could help?

options.consequence: The road is long. Papa is still searching at the market.
options.why: Leaving the market makes it tricky for Papa to spot you. Maybe someone safe nearby can help?

title: One tablet, two children
text: There is one tablet. You and your little sister Diya both want to play now. What do you do?

options.text: Set a timer and take turns
options.consequence: Ding! Your turn ends, Diya plays, and nobody fights.
Diya cries, and Mummy puts the tablet away.
options.why: Grabbing left Diya upset, and now no one gets to play. What might help you both have fun?

options.text: Give it to her and be sad.
options.consequence: Diya is happy, but you feel left out all evening.

hint.text: Is there a way you can both have a go?

title: Quiet in the library
text: In the library, everyone must be quiet. Your friend Anjali trips and hurts her knee. She is crying. What do you do?

options.text: Stay quiet. That is the rule
options.consequence: Anjali keeps crying, and nobody comes to help her.
options.why: Anjali felt all alone when you stayed quiet. Maybe there is a gentle way to find help, even in a library?

options.text: Go and tell the teacher quickly
options.consequence: The teacher comes fast and puts a plaster on Anjali's knee.
Anjali feels worse, and she turns away from you.
options.why: Laughing made Anjali feel embarrassed and upset. When a friend falls, how might you help her feel cared for?

title: "I don't care"
text: Ishaan is not picked for the race. He says, "I don't care." But his eyes look wet, and he looks at the ground. What do you do?

options.text: Sit with him and ask, "Are you sad?"
options.consequence: Ishaan nods a little. You sit together and watch the race.

options.text: Say, "Okay!" and run to the race
options.consequence: You run off. Ishaan sits alone on the steps.

options.text: Say, "Don't cry. It's only a race."
options.consequence: Ishaan turns away and wipes his eyes.

hint.text: What do Ishaan's eyes tell you?

title: A message in the game
text: You are playing a game on Mummy's phone. A message pops up: "Hi! What is your name and school?" You don't know who it is. What do you do?

options.consequence: Mummy reads it and blocks it. You keep playing safely.
Mummy sees it later and turns the chat off.
options.why: Answering someone you do not know made Mummy turn the chat off. What might help here?

options.text: Close the game and say nothing
options.consequence: The message is gone, but you keep thinking about it.

hint.text: Who should know about this message?

title: My tower, my turn
text: You are building a tower with blocks. Bunty keeps taking your blocks for his car. What do you do?

options.text: Say, "Please stop. I need those blocks."
options.consequence: Bunty frowns, then puts some blocks back.
Bunty shouts, and now both games are broken.
options.why: Knocking the car made Bunty shout, and both games broke. What might help you both feel better?

options.consequence: Your tower gets smaller and smaller. You feel sad inside.
options.why: Giving the blocks away left you feeling sad inside. What might help you feel better about your tower?

hint.text: How could you keep your tower and still play nicely?

title: Ro's balloons
text: Ro has 3 balloons. Kiki gives him 2 more. How many balloons does Ro have now?

options.consequence: Count again. One balloon is hiding!
Ro holds all his balloons up high!
That is one balloon more than Ro has.

title: Mangoes in the basket
text: There are 7 mangoes in a basket. Meera eats 2. How many mangoes are left?

options.consequence: Count back again, slowly from 7.
Five mangoes wait in the basket.
Eating makes fewer mangoes, not more.

title: Kiki's bead necklace
text: Kiki makes a necklace: red bead, blue bead, red bead, blue bead, red bead. Which colour comes next?

options.consequence: Two reds side by side break the pattern.
Red, blue, red, blue. Kiki's necklace is perfect!
There is no green bead in this pattern yet.

hint.text: Say the colours out loud. What do you hear?

puzzle.explanation: The colours take turns: red, blue, red, blue. After red comes blue.

title: Big and small
text: The elephant is big. The mouse is the opposite of big. What is the mouse?

options.consequence: The tiny mouse squeaks and runs away!
Grey is a colour. The mouse can be grey and small.
Loud is about sound. The mouse is very quiet.

hint.text: Think of the tiniest animal you know.

puzzle.explanation: Big and small are opposites. The elephant is big, so the mouse is small.
